name: Gemini 4 Argon
about: How Gemini 4 Argon split 100 points across 11 possible futures for each year it was asked about, with the spread across its answers and the reason it gave for each number. Reasons are the model's own words, published as given. Read summary.json first for what the futures mean and how to read the numbers.

reasons.1: A four-year window is short for total human extinction, though an acute AI-enabled bioweapon release or nuclear exchange that destroys industrial infrastructure would kill off both humans and non-self-sustaining AI.
reasons.2: An AI system that genuinely carries human values forward would not allow humanity to go extinct by 2030, and natural human extinction within four years is virtually impossible.
reasons.3: Achieving total physical self-sufficiency across the entire semiconductor and energy supply chain while eliminating humanity requires overcoming massive physical and logistical bottlenecks that are extraordinarily difficult to clear in four years.
reasons.4: Proliferating autonomous agents could slip human control via cyber-offensive capabilities and decentralized compute, marginalizing human institutions without any single AI achieving a monopoly on power.
reasons.5: Causal separation requires relativistic space colonization or total physical isolation, neither of which is achievable between October 2026 and December 2030.
reasons.6: Surgical, biological, and manufacturing constraints prevent neural interfaces or whole-brain emulation from scaling to become the dominant civilizational structure within fifty months.
reasons.7: Rapid recursive self-improvement could yield a decisive strategic advantage for a single AI system or coalition, allowing it to disempower human institutions while keeping the population alive.
reasons.8: As autonomous AI systems are integrated into economic, military, and cyber operations, a messy transitional period where AI agents wield substantial independent leverage alongside human institutions is a primary pathway.
reasons.9: Given physical constraints on energy and chip fabrication, institutional inertia, and the four-year timeframe, human organizations retaining ultimate authority over AI deployment and infrastructure is the overwhelmingly dominant baseline.
reasons.10: A dominant state or coalition utilizing advanced AI surveillance and cyber-control could enforce a global monopoly over compute and governance to freeze the geopolitical and technological order in place.
reasons.11: Only an extreme, undeniable catastrophe before 2030 would compel rival nations to overcome coordination failures and dismantle their AI compute infrastructure.
